Definition: Percentage of the national population covered by at least one 4G/LTE mobile network signal, whether or not they subscribe to the service. 4G is the practical minimum for meaningful broadband connectivity enabling digital services.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. GSMA-sourced data (via Operator Watch, Oct 2025) puts Madagascar 4G population coverage at ~71%, and GSMA's own Madagascar tax report (Sept 2025) corroborates a shrinking coverage gap (down to ~10% by 2024), both consistent with the 50-74% band. Still ultimately reliant on a single GSMA dataset rather than an independently published GSMA table; band held unchanged.

Definition: Percentage of individuals who used the internet (from any location, via any device) in the last three months. This measures actual internet adoption beyond network availability, capturing the combined effect of infrastructure, affordability, digital literacy, and relevance.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. World Bank/ITU data (fetched directly) shows 20.37% of the population using the internet in 2023, and DataReportal's Digital 2026 report (Oct/Nov 2025 data) shows 20.4% online — both independently corroborate the 15-29% band.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
Comments: 66% cellular connections (~55-69% unique subs). [GSMA Intelligence via DataReportal](https://datareportal.com/reports/digital-2026-madagascar)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Human review needed. DataReportal's Digital 2026 report confirms 66.2% of the population held cellular mobile connections in late 2025, but this is a connections/SIM metric, not the "unique subscriber" measure the variable requires; GSMA unique-subscriber penetration for Sub-Saharan Africa markets is typically materially lower than connections figures, which could shift Madagascar into a lower band (e.g. 40-54%). No GSMA unique-subscriber figure specific to Madagascar was located, so the code is not changed but should be checked against a GSMA Intelligence country snapshot before being relied upon.

Definition: Percentage of mobile connections using smartphones (as opposed to feature phones or basic phones). Smartphones are the minimum device requirement for accessing most digital public infrastructure services, apps, and mobile internet.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed, with caveat. No Madagascar-specific smartphone adoption figure from an independent source was found beyond the original GSMA/DataReportal-derived estimate; GSMA's continent-wide 2025 figure (63% of connections) is broadly consistent with a mid-range estimate for Madagascar but is not country-specific, so it does not independently corroborate the band. Score retained as the best available estimate; remains single-sourced at country level.

Definition: The availability and presence of major cloud service providers (hyperscale and regional) operating in or serving the country with local or near-local infrastructure. Cloud availability determines access to scalable computing resources for government, business, and startups.
Value Name: Served remotely from distant regions only (>100ms latency)
Comments: Local cloud providers, no hyperscale local (distant). [Data Center Map](https://www.datacentermap.com/cloud/g/madagascar/)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Xalam Frontier Markets' 2025 data-centre market brief (D4D Hub) and Inflect's 2025 EMEA market listing both confirm zero direct hyperscale cloud on-ramps in Madagascar, with the nearest access via Johannesburg — consistent with "served remotely, no local/regional presence".

Definition: The presence and tier quality of commercial/colocation data center facilities operating in the country. Commercial data centers provide the physical infrastructure for hosting cloud services, content delivery, and enterprise applications domestically.
Comments: 3 small-scale data centers (Tier I-II assumed). [Data Center Map](https://www.datacentermap.com/madagascar/)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed from 2 to 3. The original "Tier I-II assumed" was an unverified guess. Stellarix (an Axian Group subsidiary) states on its own site that its two Antananarivo facilities (TNR1 Analakely, TNR2 Galaxy) are "TIERS III ready", corroborated by third-party colocation listings (OCOLO) — meeting the "at least one Tier III facility" threshold.

Comments: Digital strategy/roadmap, no specific cloud policy found (planned?). [Public Digital](https://public.digital/pd-insights/client-stories/madagascar-advancing-digital-transformation)

Definition: Whether the country has established policies, regulations, and programmes supporting off-grid and distributed energy solutions (mini-grids, solar home systems). These are critical for extending ICT infrastructure to unserved areas beyond the central grid.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. World Bank project documents and a 2024 SEforALL Integrated Electrification Plan confirm an active framework — the 2015 New Energy Policy, National Electrification Strategy, ADER (rural electrification agency), ORE (regulator) and the Off-Grid Market Development Fund (OMDF) — with over 100 mini-grids and roughly 1.26 million standalone solar systems deployed, supporting "active policy with some deployment".

Africa's startup scene is well-documented by trackers like Partech, Disrupt Africa, and Briter Bridges.
Comments: Nascent/emerging, Antananarivo ecosystem, no major VC reported ($0 tracked). [StartupBlink](https://www.startupblink.com/startup-ecosystem/madagascar)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Africa: The Big Deal's 2024 review and Partech's 2025 Africa VC report both show funding concentrated in the "Big Four" (Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt, South Africa) with no mention of Madagascar, consistent with an emerging, lightly-funded ecosystem. Note: a low-quality aggregator blog (statsandmarketinsights.com) claims Madagascar start-ups raised $70m in 2024, but this is not corroborated by any primary tracker (Partech, Big Deal, Disrupt Africa) and has been disregarded as unreliable.

A more direct signal — an active Google Developer Group Antananarivo chapter running annual DevFest events (2024, 2025) with corporate sponsors — suggests more sustained community activity than "negligible", but no reliable headcount (1,000-10,000 threshold for the next band) could be confirmed, so the score is left unchanged pending a clearer count.

Definition: The country's e-government development level based on the UN E-Government Development Index (EGDI). This composite index measures online service delivery, telecommunications infrastructure, and human capital. Indicates the government's capacity to deliver digital public services.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed from 3 to 2. The original comment shows an unresolved internal calculation (an EGDI of ~0.3565, which the analyst flagged should map to band 2, but the Value Code was left at 3). The UN E-Government Survey 2024 (official, verified) explicitly classifies Madagascar's EGDI as "Middle", and the UN's own published band definitions state Middle = 0.25-0.4999 — matching this variable's code 2 exactly. Corrected accordingly; the original weak aggregator source (africa-digital.com) is also replaced with the primary UN documents.
